page: Google Cloud Platform e2-micro is an entry-level shared-core virtual machine within the general-purpose E2 family. It operates on an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.2 GHz, allocating two vCPUs backed by one-eighth of a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled. Total system memory is provisioned at 1.0 GB, which equals 0.5 GB per vCPU, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The instance includes no bundled local storage, provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and does not support GPU acceleration.

Synthetic benchmarks place the instance within the lower tier of cloud performance metrics. In compute testing, it recorded a stress-ng single-core score of 132.9, a multi-core score of 171.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 201.56. Memory testing demonstrated 9.73 GB/sec throughput for cached small-block reads, tapering to 0.1 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 1.33 GB/sec for writes. Application-level evaluation produced 0.2 million Redis SET operations per second and static web serving throughput of 0.17 GB/sec, reflecting the physical limits of fractional core scheduling.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the fractional core model provides an economical footprint for processes with low baseline CPU utilization. The primary engineering tradeoff is the 1.0 GB memory ceiling combined with burstable, shared processor time, which causes throttling under sustained computational load. This profile aligns with minimal background tasks, jump hosts, light automation scripts, continuous integration polling agents, and low-traffic staging environments.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-micro is a budget-tier virtual machine featuring two shared vCPUs mapped to one-eighth of an Intel Xeon physical core running at 2.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The machine supplies 1.0 GB of memory without bundled local storage or GPU hardware. In synthetic benchmark testing, overall output aligns with the bottom decile of evaluated servers, producing a PassMark CPU score of 201.56, a multi-core stress-ng score of 171.0, and 0.2 million Redis SET operations per second. Its restricted 1.0 GB RAM capacity and fractional compute allocation necessitate lightweight execution footprints. The instance provides high qualitative cost efficiency for intermittent or idle infrastructure, making it suitable for bastion hosts, lightweight background automation, test sandboxes, and low-traffic network services.
